item.text: South Australia’s Independent Commission Against Corruption reviewed public sector grants activity and conducted targeted evaluations of grants administration.
item.support: the Independent Commission Against Corruption undertook an information gathering exercise to better understand the grants function

item.text: The Commission found agency administration generally sound, while observing uneven practices and limited transparency across the sector.
item.support: Our initial assessment found grants administration at the agency level was generally sound.

item.text: The Commission reported that its inquiries revealed no critical or systemic integrity risks, but identified opportunities to strengthen governance.
item.support: while no critical or systemic risks to the integrity of grants activity in South Australia were revealed by the Commission’s inquiries

item.text: It suggested broader grants guidance and stronger accountability for public spending, including ministerial grant decisions, without making recommendations to specific agencies.
item.support: Reform of Treasurer’s Instruction 15 to establish accountability for public officers (including Ministers) for their grants decision making

item.quote: The legal framework and governance arrangements for public sector grants are minimal.
